source reuse is largely legitimate because claims concern different events.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Both cooperation/restraint and adverse diplomatic consequences or contested neutrality are represented.","missing_source_type":"Independent outcome assessments of diplomatic initiatives and security-cooperation effects are limited.","official_claim_independence":"Official statements dominate policy-position evidence, but AP and SIPRI provide independent checks for selected events and spending.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Not applicable or not materially evidenced for this chapter.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Military spending and security cooperation are contextualized, but civilian exposure, inherited diplomatic constraints, and external war or migration shocks are only partly developed.","supporting_evidence_ids":["WEB-2B-001","WEB-2B-002","WEB-2B-003","WEB-2B-004","WEB-2B-005","WEB-2B-006"],"unresolved_risks":["Diplomatic rhetoric and initiatives are better evidenced than results.","Shared authority and external shocks limit attribution for security outcomes.","The chapter lacks independent evidence on civilian costs of security cooperation."]},"chapter_id":"2B","defensible_evidence_estimate":6,"independent_source_family_estimate":5,"missing_themes":["Independent outcome evidence for mediation, bilateral security cooperation, and military-role expansion.","Civilian and regional exposure to the security policies described."],"substantive_issues":["The evidence is adequate for presenting policy conduct and contrary positions, but not for effectiveness or broader consequences.","No continuation is required because the principal remaining gaps are outcome-evaluation gaps not clearly recoverable from the bounded handoff."]},{"attribution_risk":"high","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"The ledger usually labels allegations, official acknowledgments, monitoring findings, and unresolved legal outcomes separately; Ayotzinapa and military-abuse claims still require careful qualification.","closed_system_silence":"High risk: military opacity, incomplete registries, threats to journalists, and weak investigations could suppress evidence of misconduct.","duplicate_reporting":"Ayotzinapa, military expansion, homicides, and press attacks recur across records; the canonical ledger mostly consolidates them, but chapter excerpts risk repeated underlying facts.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Adverse evidence is substantial, but favorable government measures and declining homicide rates are present; breadth of adverse local-language and case-level searches is not demonstrated.","missing_source_type":"More primary case files, final prosecutorial outcomes, military records, detention-registry audits, and independent local-language monitoring are needed.","official_claim_independence":"Independent UN, IACHR, HRW, Amnesty, Article 19, AP, and INEGI checks are present; official security explanations remain incompletely tested.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Press-attack counts may reflect reporting and monitoring intensity as well as underlying harm; no denominator or trend-method comparison is supplied.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Homicide and disappearance exposure are measured, but federal, state, municipal, criminal, inherited, and post-pandemic factors are not consistently separated.","supporting_evidence_ids":["WEB-3B-001","WEB-3B-002","WEB-3B-003","WEB-3B-004","WEB-3B-005","WEB-3B-006","WEB-3B-007","WEB-3B-008"],"unresolved_risks":["Military and executive attribution is strong for policy but weaker for individual abuses.","Several outcomes span years before or after 2023.","Legal and investigative endpoints are missing for important events."]},"chapter_id":"3B","defensible_evidence_estimate":8,"independent_source_family_estimate":7,"missing_themes":["Final findings and remedies for military shootings, detention, Ayotzinapa, and gender-violence cases.","Independent account of state versus federal versus criminal perpetrators.","Local-language and case-level evidence on registry omissions and investigation quality."],"substantive_issues":["The chapter has material research-recoverable attribution and event-outcome gaps.","High evidence volume does not resolve military opacity or whether formal responsibility translated into knowledge, tolerance, or remedy."]},{"attribution_risk":"medium","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"Court rulings and documented presidential statements are separated from allegations; the 2024 allegation is correctly context-only.","closed_system_silence":"High risk: executive influence, INAI paralysis, military opacity, and intimidation can suppress evidence of misconduct and concealment.","duplicate_reporting":"INAI paralysis, presidential hostility, and transparency complaints are related but distinct; government project and program claims remain self-interested and incompletely corroborated.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Not materially assessed; homicide figures are outcome data, while project complaints or affected-community reporting are absent.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Security exposure, shared authority, and inherited poverty are partly addressed;
